items.stem: What is meant by protoplasm?
items.answer: The living substance of the cell, consisting of the cytoplasm and the nucleus
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Protoplasm – the living substance of the cell, consisting of the cytoplasm and the nucleus.

items.stem: Which statement is part of the cell theory?
items.answer: New cells arise from pre-existing cells
items.markingKey: (a) New cells arise from pre-existing cells.
options: New cells arise from pre-existing cells

items.stem: Classify these as obeying the cell theory or not: Amoeba, a virus, a mango leaf, a bacterium. Give a reason for the exception.
items.answer: Obey: Amoeba, mango leaf, bacterium (all made of cells). Exception: virus, which is not made of cells.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: classification. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem: Why did Hooke see only empty boxes in cork?
items.answer: Cork is made of dead cells; only the cell walls remain, without cytoplasm or nucleus.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: dead cells. 1 mark: only walls remain.

items.stem: How did improvements in lenses change biology between Hooke (1665) and Brown (1831)?
items.answer: Better lenses gave higher magnification and clearer images, allowing observation of living cells, single-celled organisms and finally the nucleus, which led to the cell theory.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per valid link (max 3).

items.stem: Which scientist proposed that all plants and animals are composed of cells (cell theory, 1838–39)?
items.answer: Schleiden and Schwann
items.markingKey: (c) Schleiden and Schwann proposed that all plants and animals are composed of cells (cell theory, 1838–39).

items.stem: The cells in cork observed by Robert Hooke were:
items.answer: dead cells with only cell walls
items.markingKey: (a) dead cells with only cell walls.
options: dead cells with only cell walls

items.stem: Why are viruses not considered to fit the cell theory, and why do they still interest biologists?
items.answer: They are not made of cells and cannot reproduce outside a host cell; but inside cells they reproduce using the cell's machinery, showing a property of life.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: not cellular. 1 mark: reproduce only in host. 1 mark: link to life.

items.stem: Define osmosis.
items.answer: The movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Osmosis – the movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration.

items.stem: An animal cell placed in distilled water will most likely:
items.answer: swell and may burst
items.markingKey: (a) swell and may burst.

items.stem: Why is the plasma membrane called selectively permeable?
items.answer: It allows some substances such as water, oxygen and carbon dioxide to pass but prevents others.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: allows some. 1 mark: blocks others.

items.stem: For a plant cell, which of these is a hypotonic solution?
items.answer: tap water (very dilute)
items.markingKey: (a) Tap water (very dilute) is a hypotonic solution. The others: strong sugar syrup – a hypertonic solution; concentrated salt solution – a hypertonic solution; brine – a hypertonic solution.

items.stem: Predict what happens when a deshelled egg is kept in distilled water for some hours. Explain using osmosis.
items.answer: It swells.
items.markingKey: Distilled water is hypotonic to the cells, so water moves into them by osmosis through the selectively permeable membrane (1 + 1 marks).

items.stem:
Read: Students placed onion peels in three watch glasses: A with water, B with a strong salt solution and C with water after boiling the peel. After 20 minutes, under the microscope, cells in B showed the coloured contents pulled away from the cell wall; A and C cells looked normal.
(i) Name the change seen in B. (ii) Why did it occur? (iii) What will happen if B peels are put back in water? (iv) Why did boiled peels (C) not show this change in salt solution, if tried?
items.answer: (i) Plasmolysis. (ii) Water left the cells by osmosis into the hypertonic salt solution. (iii) The cells regain water and become turgid (deplasmolysis). (iv) Boiling kills cells; the membrane is no longer selectively permeable, so osmosis does not occur.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: For a plant cell, which of these is a hypotonic solution?
items.answer: distilled water
items.markingKey: (c) Distilled water is a hypotonic solution. The others: strong sugar syrup – a hypertonic solution; brine – a hypertonic solution; concentrated salt solution – a hypertonic solution.

items.stem: Predict what happens when a raisin is kept in distilled water for some hours. Explain using osmosis.
items.answer: It swells.
items.markingKey: Distilled water is hypotonic to the cells, so water moves into them by osmosis through the selectively permeable membrane (1 + 1 marks).

items.stem: For a plant cell, which of these is a hypertonic solution?

items.stem: Design an experiment with potato cups to show osmosis. Include a control.
items.answer: Make three hollow potato cups in water troughs: A empty, B with sugar, C boiled potato with sugar. After some hours water rises in B only; A shows no change (control), C shows none because boiled cells are dead.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: set-up. 1 mark: control(s). 1 mark: result and conclusion.

items.stem: Predict what happens when a raisin is kept in concentrated salt solution for some hours. Explain using osmosis.
items.answer: It shrinks / becomes limp (loses water).
items.markingKey: Concentrated salt solution is hypertonic to the cells, so water moves out of them by osmosis through the selectively permeable membrane (1 + 1 marks).

items.stem:
Read: An electron micrograph of a liver cell shows many mitochondria, much smooth ER and many lysosomes, while a pancreas cell shows a lot of rough ER and a large Golgi apparatus.
(i) Which organelle releases energy? (ii) Why does the liver cell have much smooth ER? (iii) Why does the pancreas cell have a lot of rough ER and Golgi? (iv) Name the organelle that digests worn-out parts.
items.answer: (i) Mitochondria. (ii) Smooth ER helps in detoxifying poisons and drugs and making lipids, which is the liver's work. (iii) It makes and secretes digestive enzymes (proteins); rough ER makes them and Golgi packages and dispatches them. (iv) Lysosomes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Why are lysosomes called suicide bags?
items.answer: When a cell is damaged, its lysosomes may burst and their enzymes digest the cell itself.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: enzymes. 1 mark: digest own cell.

items.stem: Explain how the ER, ribosomes and Golgi apparatus work together to make and send out a protein such as an enzyme.
items.answer: Ribosomes on the rough ER make the protein; the ER carries it to the Golgi; the Golgi modifies and packages it into vesicles that leave the cell.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per organelle role in sequence.

items.stem: A cell has no nucleus. Can it divide? Give an example of such a cell and explain how it survives.
items.answer: No, it cannot divide; mature red blood cells of mammals have no nucleus, survive about 120 days and are replaced by new cells made in the bone marrow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cannot divide. 1 mark: RBC example. 1 mark: replacement.

items.stem: What would happen to a cell if its Golgi apparatus stopped working?
items.answer: Proteins and other materials made in the cell would not be packaged and dispatched; secretion would stop and new lysosomes would not form.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: packaging stops. 1 mark: secretion/lysosomes affected.

items.stem: Which organelle is NOT bound by a membrane?
items.answer: Ribosome
items.markingKey: (c) Ribosome.

items.stem: What is the main function of the ribosomes?
items.answer: Are the sites of protein synthesis
items.markingKey: (d) The ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.

Is a network of membrane-bound tubes that transports materials; the rough type makes proteins
Contain digestive enzymes that break down worn-out cell parts and foreign material
Are the sites of protein synthesis

items.answer: A name for lysosomes, because they can digest their own cell when it is damaged
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Suicide bags – a name for lysosomes, because they can digest their own cell when it is damaged.
